description: Helps you decide which customer segment to back, and whether your pricing is safe if AI cuts seats: it takes each segment's ACV, sales cycle, accounts, deal source and CAC, its logo, gross and net retention, how you charge in your own words, and your seller ramp, cost and qualified demand, and returns one page per segment with payback, gross profit per dollar of CAC, seller capacity after ramp and cycle, and the renewal if customers cut a share of seats. Ask the person to confirm the segment split, their own win rate and what customers can cut before marking each as confirmed; anything not confirmed or not given is shown as missing, never guessed. Read-only for business data. It needs no sign-in and stores no inputs or outputs. Hosted usage metadata is recorded. Missing required fields or invalid values return an error naming what to supply or correct. Use this instead of scale_paid_check when you need segment economics, seller capacity and seat-reduction scenarios.

business_stage.description: Optional: funding stage, passed to the motion first draft (for example series-a). Format is text.

confirmed.description: What the person has confirmed. Set each to true only after asking them. Until the segment split is confirmed no sum runs. Format is a JSON object. For example, {"segment_split":true,"win_rate":true,"seat_cut":true}.

seat_cut.description: The person confirmed what customers can cut, and the share of seats to test. Format is true or false. For example, true.

segment_split.description: The person confirmed the segments are how their closed deals really divide. Format is true or false. For example, true.

win_rate.description: The person confirmed the win rates are their own, from closed deals. Format is true or false. For example, true.

gross_margin_percent.description: Gross margin as a percent (for example 72). Needed for payback and every profit sum. Format is a JSON number.

industry.description: Optional: your industry, passed to the motion first draft. Format is text. For example, "manufacturing".

product.description: What you sell, in one line. Format is text. For example, "invoice review service".

segments.description: One item per customer segment (1 to 4). Split by who signs, how they find you, sales cycle and contract value. Format is a JSON array. For example, [{"name":"an approved anonymous manufacturer"}].

items.description: Format is a JSON object. For example, {"name":"an approved anonymous manufacturer"}.

accounts.description: Number of accounts that could buy in this segment. Format is a JSON number. For example, 12.

acv.description: Average contract value per year, in dollars. Format is a JSON number. For example, 24000.

arr_share_cutting_percent.description: Optional: the percent of this segment's revenue held by accounts that would make that cut (for example 32). Format is a JSON number.

buyer_cost_per_seat_per_year.description: Optional: what one seat costs the buyer in a year, in salary and overhead, in dollars. Format is a JSON number. For example, 24000.

cac.description: Cost to win one customer in this segment, in dollars. Format is a JSON number. For example, 24000.

churn_reasons.description: Optional: why customers in this segment leave or shrink, in their words, separated by semicolons. Format is text. For example, "implementation delays and unclear ownership".

deal_source.description: Where most deals in this segment come from (for example inbound, outbound, referrals, partnerships or mixed). Format is text.

gross_retention_gate_percent.description: Optional: your own gross retention line for releasing more money (for example 90). Format is a JSON number.

gross_retention_percent.description: Gross revenue retention as a percent: opening revenue less churn and downgrades, over opening revenue (for example 92). It cannot pass 100. Format is a JSON number.

icp_match_percent.description: Optional: percent of accounts that match your ideal customer profile, passed to the sizing first draft. Format is a JSON number. For example, 30.

logo_retention_gate_percent.description: Optional: your own logo retention line (for example 85). Format is a JSON number.

logo_retention_percent.description: Share of customers still paying after a year, as a percent (for example 89). Format is a JSON number.

monthly_logo_churn_percent.description: Optional: share of customers lost in a month, as a percent (for example 2.5). Used for the simple lifetime sum; left out, yearly logo retention is used. Format is a JSON number.

monthly_qualified_demand.description: Qualified opportunities assigned to sellers each month in this segment. Format is a JSON number. For example, 12.

motion_lead.description: Optional: the lead motion from the EPIC audit on GTM Alpha, as it came back. Format is text. For example, "E".

motion_reason.description: Optional: the audit's reason line for the lead motion, as it came back. Format is text. For example, "buyers rely on partner referrals".

motion_score.description: Optional: the score of that lead motion, 1 to 10. Format is a JSON number. For example, 10.

name.description: The segment in your own words (for example 'banks and insurers with 200 to 2,000 contact centre agents'). Format is text.

net_retention_gate_percent.description: Optional: your own net retention line (for example 100). Format is a JSON number.

net_retention_percent.description: Net revenue retention as a percent: gross retention plus expansion (for example 108). Format is a JSON number.

pricing_unit.description: Optional: the pricing unit, if you want to state it directly. It overrides the reading of your sentence. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "seat".

pricing_unit_in_writing.description: What you bill on, in your own words (for example 'per agent seat, billed yearly' or 'per resolved contact'). Format is text.

ramped_deals_per_seller_per_year.description: Deals a fully ramped seller closes in a year in this segment, from your own record. Format is a JSON number. For example, 12.

run_cost_per_unit.description: Optional: your cost to run one unit of work, in dollars. Format is a JSON number. For example, 24000.

sales_cycle_days.description: Days from first meeting to signature. Format is a JSON number. For example, 12.

seat_cut_percent.description: Optional: the percent of seats a customer could cut if AI does more of the work (for example 25). Used only when the person has confirmed it. Format is a JSON number.

seat_share_of_acv_percent.description: Optional, for a mix of seats and usage: the percent of the contract billed on seats (for example 60). Format is a JSON number.

seats_per_account.description: Optional: seats in an average account. Format is a JSON number. For example, 12.

seller_loaded_cost_per_year.description: Full yearly cost of one seller, in dollars. Format is a JSON number. For example, 24000.

seller_ramp_months.description: Months before a new seller carries a full pipeline. Format is a JSON number. For example, 12.

sizing_sam.description: Optional: SAM in dollars from the sizing calculator. Format is a JSON number. For example, 12.

sizing_som.description: Optional: year one SOM in dollars from the sizing calculator. Format is a JSON number. For example, 12.

sizing_tam.description: Optional: TAM in dollars from the sizing calculator on ICP Intelligence. Format is a JSON number. For example, 12.

sizing_year_one_customers.description: Optional: customers needed in year one, from the sizing calculator. Format is a JSON number. For example, 12.

usage_price_per_unit.description: Optional: a price per unit of work you want to test, in dollars. Format is a JSON number. For example, 24000.

what_customers_can_cut.description: What a customer can cut, and when, in your own words (for example 'seats, at each yearly renewal'). Format is text.

win_rate_percent.description: Your own win rate: the percent of qualified opportunities you win in this segment, from your closed deals (for example 33). Used only when the person has confirmed it. Format is a JSON number.

work_units_per_seat_per_year.description: Optional: units of work one seat handles in a year (for example contacts, shipments or claims). Format is a JSON number.

year_one_customer_target.description: Optional: new customers you want from this segment in year one. Left out, the customer count from the sizing first draft is used. Format is a JSON number. For example, 12.

year_one_share_percent.description: Optional: the year one share you assume, as a percent, passed to the sizing first draft. Format is a JSON number. For example, 30.

tracks_expansion.description: Optional: true only if the company tracks expansion account by account. It adds a later years table below the pages. Payback on CAC and ARR always leads. Format is true or false. For example, true.

name: segment_and_seat_cut_check
title: Segment and Seat Cut Check
